entry.text:
Q1: src/hub.ts:65 `static DEFAULT_NUDGE_MS = Number(process.env.CHATROOM_NUDGE_AFTER_MS ?? 180_000)`; applied hub.ts:94. Takes effect (a) silence nudge armNudge hub.ts:1036-1060, re-armed by every post() hub.ts:985 (incl. system posts), identical nudge max 2x (1054-1055); (b) openings deadline hub.ts:136 (2 periods at creation), 1081 (1 period from first opening, chat doesn't reset), 1092-1108 (unarrived -> warn + one more period); (c) server.ts:325,442,464 hints report it in minutes. persistence.ts:77 legacy default 180_000. Verdict: keep — with 9 seats any message resets the silence timer so the nudge only fires on genuine stalls; the openings deadline already extends for unarrived seats; shorter would hurry seats mid-research, longer would idle 8 seats on one slow opener.
Q2: offlineScripts array scripts/offline-runner.mjs:26-182. Only 'bench-build-oracle-audit.test.ts' (lines 64 and 78). seat-env-regression.ts (158) and claude-lean-flags-regression.ts (88) appear once in the list; their second grep hit is line 192 (the --experimental-vm-modules condition), outside the list. Confirmed by importing offlineScripts in node: 155 entries, only that duplicate.
Q3: src/server.ts:21 `MAX_WAIT_MS = 55_000; // stay under typical MCP client tool timeouts (Codex 60s)`; enforced server.ts:348 (zod max) and 359 (min). Justified: 5s headroom under Codex's 60s; DEFAULT_WAIT_MS (line 20) is equal so the default never exceeds the cap; our own seat client uses 180s (seat.ts:418) but the cap protects external clients.

proposal.text:
Q1: src/hub.ts:65 sets Hub.DEFAULT_NUDGE_MS = Number(process.env.CHATROOM_NUDGE_AFTER_MS ?? 180_000) (3 min), applied per room at hub.ts:94. Verdict: KEEP 3 min for a nine-seat session. It takes effect in two places: (a) the silence nudge armNudge (hub.ts:1036-1060), re-armed on every post (hub.ts:985) and capped at two identical nudges (hub.ts:1054-1056) — with nine seats posting, true 3-minute silence is rare, so the nudge fires only when a room really has stalled, and a shorter value would add noise between seats that are reading/running tools; (b) the blind-openings deadline (hub.ts:136 two periods at creation, hub.ts:1081 one period from the first opening, hub.ts:1093-1108 warn then reveal one period later), which is NOT reset by chat — nine seats make a missing opening more likely, and a longer default would hold eight seats idle for one straggler, while a shorter one would cut off slow-starting seats. 3 min balances both; no change.
Q2: exactly one name appears more than once in the offlineScripts list: 'bench-build-oracle-audit.test.ts' (scripts/offline-runner.mjs:64 and :78). (seat-env-regression.ts and claude-lean-flags-regression.ts appear again only in the flag condition at :192, outside the list.)
Q3: src/server.ts:21 MAX_WAIT_MS = 55_000, comment "stay under typical MCP client tool timeouts (Codex 60s)"; enforced at server.ts:348 (schema max) and :359 (Math.min). Verdict: still justified, since the hub serves external/unconfigured clients whose default timeout is ~60s, but the comment is partly stale for the hub's own seats, which raise their client timeouts (codex-seat.ts:13 tool_timeout_sec=120; env.ts:35 MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT=120000). Keep the cap; the comment could note that spawned seats are configured higher.

challenge.objection: The proposal says "a shorter one would cut off slow-starting seats" but does not say that 3 minutes already cuts some off. At hub.ts:1100-1108 the extra period applies only when a seat has not joined (unarrived() > 0). A seat that joined but is still reading code when the deadline hits is revealed without its opening, because the clock starts at the first opening (:1081). The verdict holds only because a late seat can still speak in chat (:1107 message). The proposal should name that as the mitigation rather than call 3 minutes a balance with no cost.
